descricao: Eurostars Eurostars Innovation Programmes Funding for international SME-led research and development Eurostars is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . Eurostars is an international funding programme for collaborative research and development (R&D) projects led by innovative small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As the world’s largest SME R&D funding programme, Eurostars supports the creation of innovative products, processes, and services for commercialisation. How Eurostars supports you You can use Eurostars to access public funding for international R&D projects. The programme has some unique features: Work with international partners to strengthen your R&D Reduce the risk of your R&D Develop new business relationships Access international markets Be guided from idea to commercialisation with advice and support from a network of national project coordinators Eurostars provides funding to international R&D projects. Projects must be led by an SME or startup from a Eurostars country or region, and the project consortium must also include at least one other independent organisation from another Eurostars country. Partners in the consortium can include any type of organisation. Eurostars funding comes from National Funding Bodies, which are ministries or funding agencies in each Eurostars country or region, and from the European Commission. National Funding Bodies determine how much funding is available, the funding rate per type of company, and which activities are eligible based on national rules. Your project must meet seven criteria to be eligible for Eurostars funding: The project consortium must be led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country. The project consortium must be composed of at least two entities that are independent from each other. The project consortium must be composed of entities from at least two Eurostars countries. At least one of those countries must be an EU or Horizon Europe Associated Country . The budget of the SMEs from the Eurostars countries (excluding any subcontracting) is 50% or more of the total project cost. No single participant or country in the project can be responsible for more than 70% of the project’s budget. The project must have a duration of 36 months or less. The project must be exclusively focused on civil applications. The Eurostars programme uses a decentralised funding methodology. That means that organisations do not receive public funding from the Eureka Network. Instead, they receive funding directly from National Funding Bodies. This funding is granted according to national rules and procedures. Make sure that you and your project partners contact your National Funding Body to understand what national rules and procedures apply. You can find these rules, and contact details for National Funding bodies, in each call for projects. Please read all our guidelines before submitting a project application. If you do not meet all our eligibility criteria, your application will be rejected. Detailed guidelines on making an application, and the evaluation process, are available in the resource library. descricao: Innowwide Innowwide Innovation Programmes Helping SMEs go global Innowwide is funded by the European Union as part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs Innowwide supports innovative small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and startups to assess the viability of research or commercial plans in international markets. The programme offers grants of 60,000 euro. How Innowwide supports you The Innowwide programme provides grant funding to SMEs and startups so that they can run market feasibility projects in cooperation with local actors in the selected target country. Market feasibility projects allow SMEs to gain a deep understanding of the business environment in a specific target country. Some key outcomes from the project include: Understanding the technical feasibility of your product, process, or service in that market Understanding the viability of your business model Identifying key local legal, financial, political, cultural, and behavioural characteristics that could affect the deployment of your solution Identifying ideal ways to exploit your solution, including further research and innovation Funded projects receive a grant of 60,000 euro to assess the practical, technical, and economic feasibility of an innovative solution in a new market during a 6-month timeframe. Projects must come from an SME or startup in an EU Member State, Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye, or the United Kingdom. They must be directed towards a target country in: Africa, the Americas, Asia, or Oceania. You can apply if you are an SME or startups from an EU Member State, Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye or the United Kingdom. Applications to Innowwide must include an independent subcontractor that is established in the target country. Innowwide funding is awarded to one actor, specifically to the applicant SME. The partner entity is the main subcontractor for the market feasibility project. Detailed information about Innowwide is available in the resource library. If you have any questions about this Innowwide programme, please contact the Innowwide team at the Eureka Secretariat, using our contact form . Network Projects Network Projects Innovation Programmes Flexible programme for international research and development cooperation The Network Projects programme provides access to funding for international research and development projects. It is designed to be flexible, with few limitations on the organisations that can participate in a project. How Network Projects supports you This programme provides access to funding for research and development projects in a range of areas. As well as the general open call for projects, several sector, technology, or geographic specific calls are launched each year. How the Network Projects programme works Project applications can be made throughout the year and do not have to fit into any specific area of research, development or innovation. Projects are assessed by your National Funding Body. There are different types of call. A general call for projects is permanently open. National Funding Bodies also work together to launch specific calls for projects throughout the year. These calls are usually based on a particular theme or area of technology and are also often limited to certain countries. Depending on the details of the call and the country where you are applying from, support might be either as a grant or loan. Your project must meet several criteria to be eligible for funding under the Network Projects programme: Eligibility criteria Your project consortium must be made up of at least two entities that are independent from each other. Your project must be intended to research or develop a product, process, or service. Your project must be exclusively focused on civilian, non-military applications. The members of your project consortium must come from at least two participating countries. No single organisation or country can be responsible for more than 70% of the project budget. You can participate in a research and development project even if you are not eligible to receive funding. Detailed guidelines on making an application, and the evaluation process, are available in the resource library. National Funding Bodies often have additional rules about which organisations can receive funding. You can find these rules in each call for projects. descricao: Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator Innovation Programmes Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator Continue innovating and scale-up your SME The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . The Fast Track to the EIC Accelerator is designed to help startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that have completed, or are about to complete, a Eurostars-3-funded project to continue growing and developing. The scheme enables you to skip the first step (short proposal) and move directly to the second step (full proposal) of the EIC Accelerator. The EIC Accelerator supports startups, SMEs, and small mid-caps to scale up high impact innovations with the potential to create new markets or disrupt existing ones. The programme provides a unique combination of grant and investment funding, along with coaching, mentoring, and access to investors and corporates. Run by the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA), the programme focuses on deep tech innovation and patient capital. In 2026, 634 million euro has been allocated to the EIC Accelerator. If you succeed in the Fast Track, your EIC Accelerator full proposal can be submitted to any of the following cut-offs in 2026: January 7, March 4, May 6, July 8, September 2, or November 4. Eureka Network has partnered with EISMEA to create this Fast Track as part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs . How the Fast Track works The Fast Track scheme allows startups, SMEs and small mid-caps that have completed a Eurostars project to skip the first step of the EIC Accelerator application. This year, the Eureka Network will allocate 20 full proposal tickets for the EIC Accelerator to selected participants. Fast Track advantages The Fast Track has several important advantages: By skipping the first step of the EIC Accelerator application, you will compete against fewer companies. Eureka’s expert evaluators will review your project and provide you with detailed feedback. You can pitch your project to an expert panel, helping to prepare for the formal EIC Accelerator pitch. You can receive a no-risk evaluation of your project idea. Who can apply for the Fast Track You must meet several criteria to be able to apply for the Fast Track: Eligibility criteria Your organisation must be a legal entity established in an EU Member State, Iceland, Israel, Norway, Switzerland, Türkiye, or the United Kingdom. It must be a startup, SME, or a small mid-cap. You must have successfully completed a Eurostars-3 project in the two years preceding the Fast Track submission deadline, or be in the final 6 months of your project. You must have an innovative business concept derived from your Eurostars-3 project. You must own, or have the right to use, the intellectual property that your innovation is based on. More information about the eligibility criteria for Fast Track is available in the resource library. This includes information about the definition of a Eurostars-3 project. Globalstars Globalstars Innovation Programmes Access new markets with global research and development Globalstars is a programme for organisations to connect with partners outside the Eureka network. The programme supports projects between companies in Eureka countries or regions and in leading and emerging markets around the world. How Globalstars supports you Globalstars provides access to funding for research and development projects in a range of areas. As well as funding, Globalstars gives you a unique opportunity to work with organisations in countries and regions like Japan, Uruguay, India, and Taiwan. How Globalstars works Globalstars provides funding to international research and development (R&D) projects. Projects must include at least one organisation from a Eureka country or region participating in the call, and the project consortium must also include at least one other independent organisation from the Globalstars country. Partners in the consortium can include other SMEs, large companies, universities, research institutions, and non-profits. Funding for Globalstars comes from National Funding Bodies in each country or region that is participating in a call. National Funding Bodies decide which organisations can receive funding, which activities can be funded, and how much funding is available. Your project must meet several criteria to be eligible for funding under Globalstars. Eligibility criteria Your project consortium must be made up of at least two entities that are independent from each other. Your project must be intended to research or develop a product, process, or service. Your project must be exclusively focused on civilian, non-military applications. The members of your project consortium must come from at least two participating countries. At least one member must come from a Eureka country or region that is participating in the call, and one from a Globalstars country or region. No single organisation or country can be responsible for more than 70% of the project budget. You can participate in a research and development project even if you are not eligible to receive funding. Detailed guidelines on making an application, and the evaluation process, are available in the resource library. National Funding Bodies often have additional rules about which organisations can receive funding. You can find these rules in each call for projects. Investment Readiness Investment Readiness Innovation Programmes Investment Readiness The Investment Readiness programme is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . The Investment Readiness programme connects you with multinational corporates and private investors. The programme can help your startup or SME grow in a range of sectors. How Investment Readiness supports you Investment Readiness offers you the opportunity to get your solution in front of Eureka’s corporate partners. If successful, you will be invited to a meeting with the corporate to discuss future projects or investment with them. Eureka also organises missions to major international investment conferences, such as Web Summit and Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH). How Investment Readiness works The Investment Readiness programme has two main activities: Corporate Challenges Eureka’s corporate partners set Corporate Challenges that you can respond to. If you are successful, you could collaborate with the corporate in a pilot project or access investment, depending on the challenge. We organise international missions to major investment conferences. Past missions have been to Web Summit and the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology. These conferences give you the chance to meet international investors face-to-face. In 2026, we will organise three international missions for SMEs and startups to attend South Summit Brazil in Porto Alegre, Brazil from 25 to 27 March and the Swiss Biotech Days in Basel, Switzerland from 4 to 5 May. A third destination will be announced soon. Corporate Challenges See open Corporate Challenges Siemens Healthineers Verge HealthTech Fund Open calls for projects Got an innovative idea? descricao: Eurostars Call 11 for projects – deadline September 2026 Deadline 10 September 2026 Eurostars Call 11 for projects – deadline September 2026 Find out more Eurostars Call 11 for projects – deadline September 2026 Eurostars is part of the European Partnership on Innovative SMEs. The partnership is co-funded by the European Union through Horizon Europe . Countries and regions Eurostars is a funding instrument that supports innovative SMEs and project partners (large companies, universities, research organisations and other types of organisations) by funding international collaborative R&D and innovation projects. By participating, organisations can access public funding for international collaborative R&D projects in all fields. To have a successful Eurostars application you must: Define your project idea. Collaborate internationally, sharing expertise. Develop products, processes or services that can be easily commercialised. You can submit your R&D and innovation project application between 9 July 2026 and 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CET using our project platform ( myeurekaproject.org ). Your project consortium must have an innovative SME in the leading role, but it can also include other types of organisations like large companies, universities, research organisations and more. The amount of funding your organisation receives when you participate in a project is managed by your National Funding Body. Funding rules vary from country to country and your National Funding Body decides: which organisations can receive funding, which project activities can be funded If you are from a Eurostars country, you can discover what funding is available for your organisation in our ‘Country information’ section below, and by contacting your national or regional funding body using our contact form . Your National Funding Body may have maximum funding amount per project or project partner. Organisations from non-Eurostars countries can participate by self-funding their project costs. 9 July 2026: Call opens 10 September 2026, 14:00 CET: Deadline To apply, you must meet seven international eligibility criteria: The project consortium is led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country. The project consortium is composed of at least two entities that are independent of one another. The project consortium is composed of entities from at least two Eurostars countries with at least one organisation coming from an EU or Horizon Europe Associated Country The budget of the SMEs from the Eurostars countries (excluding any subcontracting) is 50% or more of the total project cost. No single participant or country is responsible for more than 70% of the budget of the project. The project duration is 36 months or less. The project has an exclusive focus on civil applications. You can find more information and definitions of the terms used in these criteria in the detailed Eurostars guidelines. Please read the guidelines and other resources before submitting a project application. If you do not meet all our international eligibility criteria, your application will be rejected. Additionally, you might need to fulfil national or regional eligibility criteria. Please check with your national or regional funding body.
